title: Chemical Splash to Skin or Eyes
summary: Prioritize decontamination, isolate the source, and activate medical escalation early.
trigger_signs: Chemical enters eyes, face, or exposed skin
Burning pain, redness, blurred vision, or damaged gloves/clothing
immediate_actions: Stop the operation and call for nearby support immediately.
Use eyewash or emergency shower continuously according to local SOP.
Remove contaminated gloves, coat, or face shield while flushing.
Bring the SDS or chemical label information for handoff.
forbidden: Do not delay flushing while searching for paperwork.
Do not neutralize on the body unless the local SOP explicitly requires it.
Do not let the exposed person continue working.
escalation: Notify supervisor and institutional emergency contact.
Seek medical evaluation for eye exposure, persistent pain, or unknown chemicals.

title: Small Laboratory Fire or Ignition
summary: Only fight a small controllable fire if trained and exit remains clear; otherwise evacuate immediately.
trigger_signs: Visible flame, burning solvent, electrical smoke, or overheated equipment
Rapid heat rise, ignition near flammables, or failed heating control
immediate_actions: Stop the process if safe, isolate gas/power, and warn nearby people.
Use the correct extinguisher only if the fire is small and you are trained.
If fire is not controlled immediately, evacuate and close the door behind you.
Report the location and material involved to emergency responders.
forbidden: Do not fight a growing fire alone.
Do not use the wrong extinguisher for solvent, metal, or electrical fire.
Do not re-enter before clearance.
ppe: Standard lab PPE for evacuation support
Thermal or specialized PPE only for trained responders
escalation: Trigger the institutional fire alarm and emergency call chain.
Record involved chemicals, gases, and cylinders for responder briefing.

title: Electrical Shock or Energized Equipment Incident
summary: Cut power first, avoid direct contact with the victim, and escalate medical support immediately.
trigger_signs: Person collapses near energized equipment
Sparks, exposed conductors, damaged insulation, or burning smell
immediate_actions: Isolate power using emergency stop, breaker, or unplug only if safe.
Use a non-conductive object to separate the victim from the source if still energized.
Call emergency medical support and monitor breathing until responders arrive.
Secure the area and preserve the equipment state for incident review.
forbidden: Do not touch the victim directly before power is isolated.
Do not re-energize or test the device after the event.
Do not ignore minor shock symptoms.
escalation: Immediate medical evaluation is required after electrical exposure.
Notify equipment owner and safety manager before restart or repair.

title: Chemical Spill or Leak
summary: Assess size and toxicity quickly, isolate the zone, and use the spill SOP instead of improvised cleanup.
trigger_signs: Liquid on bench or floor, broken container, spreading odor, or visible vapor
Unknown substance outside containment or damaged transport container
immediate_actions: Stop nearby work, isolate the area, and identify the material if possible.
Use spill kit, absorbent, or containment tools only if the spill is within your training level.
Increase local ventilation if the SOP allows and exposure risk is manageable.
Package contaminated absorbents and waste according to the waste route.
forbidden: Do not touch unknown material with bare hands.
Do not wash incompatible chemicals into the drain without approval.
Do not continue nearby ignition or heat-generating work.
ppe: Respiratory protection if required by SOP
escalation: Escalate immediately for large, unknown, toxic, or highly volatile spills.
Report the material, quantity, and exposure status to the supervisor and safety contact.

title: Thermal Burn or Scald Injury
summary: Cool the burn immediately with running water, protect the wound, and seek medical evaluation for severe burns.
trigger_signs: Skin contact with hot surface, boiling liquid, steam, or heated glassware
Redness, blistering, charring, or severe pain at contact site
immediate_actions: Cool the burn under cool running water for at least 15 minutes.
Remove clothing or jewelry near the burn area if not stuck to skin.
Cover the burn with a clean, non-stick dressing or cling film.
Seek medical attention for burns larger than a palm, on face/joints, or deep burns.
forbidden: Do not apply ice, butter, oil, toothpaste, or home remedies to the burn.
Do not pop blisters or remove clothing stuck to the burn.
Do not ignore burns that appear minor — depth may not be immediately visible.
escalation: Immediate medical evaluation for full-thickness burns, facial burns, or electrical/chemical burns.
Notify supervisor and record the cause, material, and temperature involved.

title: Cut, Puncture, or Bleeding Injury
summary: Control bleeding with direct pressure, protect the wound from contamination, and escalate for deep or uncontrolled wounds.
trigger_signs: Active bleeding from glass breakage, blade cut, needle stick, or sharp equipment
Embedded foreign object, pulsatile bleeding, or numbness beyond the wound
immediate_actions: Apply direct pressure to the wound with clean gauze or cloth.
Elevate the injured area above heart level if possible.
For minor cuts, clean with water, apply antiseptic, and bandage.
For embedded objects, stabilize in place — do not remove.
forbidden: Do not remove embedded glass, metal, or needle fragments.
Do not wash deep or heavily bleeding wounds under running water.
Do not ignore needlestick injuries — always report and seek follow-up.
ppe: Nitrile or examination gloves for responders
Eye protection if blood splash risk exists
escalation: Seek immediate medical care for uncontrolled bleeding, deep wounds, or needlestick exposure.
Report all sharps injuries per institutional protocol; preserve the object for identification.

title: Gas Leak or Toxic Vapor Exposure
summary: Evacuate immediately, shut off the gas source only if safe, and ventilate before re-entry.
trigger_signs: Unusual odor, hissing sound from cylinder or gas line, or visible vapor cloud
Sudden dizziness, headache, nausea, or breathing difficulty among multiple people
immediate_actions: Evacuate the area immediately and alert all nearby personnel.
Shut off the gas source only if it is safe to approach.
Open windows and activate ventilation from outside the affected zone.
Account for all personnel at the assembly point.
forbidden: Do not operate electrical switches, phones, or equipment that may cause sparks.
Do not re-enter until the area has been declared safe by trained personnel.
Do not attempt to locate the leak source before evacuation.
ppe: Self-contained breathing apparatus for responders only
Gas detection monitor for entry teams
escalation: Call institutional emergency number and fire department for any gas release.
Record the gas type, cylinder ID, and duration of exposure for medical handoff.

title: Cryogenic Exposure or Cold Burn (Liquid Nitrogen / Dry Ice)
summary: Treat as a thermal burn, but watch for asphyxiation risk from oxygen displacement in enclosed spaces.
trigger_signs: Skin contact with liquid nitrogen, dry ice, or ultra-cold surfaces
Waxy white or grey skin, numbness, blistering, or brittle texture at contact site
immediate_actions: Remove the cold source and warm the affected area gradually with body heat or tepid water.
Remove constrictive clothing or jewelry near the affected area.
Cover with a clean, dry dressing and seek medical evaluation.
For enclosed-space exposure, check for dizziness or confusion (oxygen depletion).
forbidden: Do not rub or massage the frozen tissue.
Do not apply direct heat, hot water, or radiant heaters to the affected area.
Do not work alone with cryogenic materials in confined spaces.
escalation: Medical evaluation required for any cryogenic burn beyond superficial redness.
Monitor for delayed symptoms if oxygen depletion was suspected.
Report the equipment, duration, and volume involved to the safety officer.

title: Centrifuge Malfunction or Rotor Failure
summary: Stop the run immediately if safe, keep the lid closed until rotation stops, and treat any aerosol release as biohazard/chemical exposure.
trigger_signs: Abnormal vibration, loud noise, or grinding sound during centrifugation
Visible imbalance, lid movement, or fluid leakage around the centrifuge
immediate_actions: Press emergency stop or power off if abnormal noise or vibration is detected.
Keep the lid closed until the rotor has completely stopped.
If aerosol release is suspected, evacuate the immediate area for 30 minutes.
After the rotor stops, inspect for tube breakage and decontaminate per SOP.
forbidden: Do not open the lid while the rotor is still spinning.
Do not attempt to balance the rotor by hand during operation.
Do not reuse a dropped rotor or one that shows visible damage.
ppe: Chemical or biohazard gloves as applicable
escalation: Report any rotor failure or tube breakage to the equipment manager for inspection.
If biohazardous or chemical aerosol is suspected, activate institutional exposure protocol.

title: Autoclave or High-Pressure Equipment Incident
summary: Never open under pressure; treat steam burns and report equipment faults immediately.
trigger_signs: Steam escaping from door seal, abnormally high pressure reading, or failure to depressurize
Sudden pop, burn from steam release, or door that cannot be opened after cycle
immediate_actions: Do not attempt to open the door — wait for pressure gauge to return to zero.
If steam burn occurs, treat as thermal burn: cool under water for 15 minutes.
Report the equipment fault and lock out the autoclave until inspected.
If load was biohazardous and containment failed, initiate biohazard spill protocol.
forbidden: Do not force the autoclave door open under any pressure.
Do not bypass safety interlocks or pressure relief devices.
Do not use a malfunctioning autoclave while waiting for repair.
ppe: Face shield when opening after cycle
escalation: Lock out and tag the equipment immediately after the incident.
Notify facility manager and safety officer before restart.
Record cycle parameters, load contents, and time of incident.

title: Biological Exposure or Biohazard Spill
summary: Contain the spill, decontaminate with appropriate disinfectant, and report any potential exposure immediately.
trigger_signs: Broken culture plate, spilled liquid culture, or aerosol release from biological sample
Needlestick with biological material, splash to mucous membranes, or broken skin contact
immediate_actions: Stop work and warn nearby personnel immediately.
Cover the spill with absorbent material soaked in appropriate disinfectant.
Allow sufficient contact time (usually 20-30 min) before cleanup.
For personal exposure, wash skin with soap and water; flush eyes/mucous membranes for 15 minutes.
forbidden: Do not leave the spill unattended without marking the area.
Do not use bleach on spills containing ammonium compounds.
Do not delay reporting a potential exposure — prophylactic treatment windows are time-sensitive.
escalation: Report exposure immediately to the biosafety officer and occupational health.
Document the agent, route of exposure, and time of incident.
Preserve the source material for identification if needed.

title: Chemical Ingestion or Hazardous Inhalation
summary: Move to fresh air for inhalation; do not induce vomiting for ingestion — follow SDS and seek immediate medical attention.
trigger_signs: Accidental drinking, pipetting by mouth (prohibited), or eating near chemicals
Coughing, choking, chest tightness, dizziness, or chemical taste in mouth
immediate_actions: For inhalation: move the person to fresh air immediately and loosen tight clothing.
For ingestion: rinse mouth with water; do NOT induce vomiting unless SDS explicitly instructs.
Bring the chemical container, label, or SDS to the medical provider.
Monitor breathing and consciousness; perform CPR if trained and needed.
forbidden: Do not induce vomiting unless the SDS or poison control specifically advises it.
Do not give anything by mouth to an unconscious person.
Do not delay seeking medical care while searching for the perfect SDS.
ppe: Nitrile gloves for responders handling contaminated items
Respiratory protection only for trained responders in high-vapor environments
escalation: Call emergency medical services or poison control immediately.
Report the chemical name, estimated quantity, route of exposure, and time.
Keep the original container and any vomitus for medical analysis.
